bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) in ELF parsing: an 8-byte read in get_ne64 / BEPolicy::get64 (src/bele.h / src/bele_policy.h), invoked from PackLinuxElf64::PackLinuxElf64help1 (src/p_lx_elf.cpp, seen during PackLinuxElf64ppc construction), can read past the end of an ELF-derived buffer when processing symbol table information. A crafted ELF input can trigger this out-of-bounds read, leading to crashes or potential disclosure of memory contents.
bug_description.normalized: The staged testcase is admitted on the 64-bit big-endian ET_DYN ELF path, so `PackLinuxElf64::PackLinuxElf64help1` allocates heap-backed `file_image`, copies the attacker-controlled file into it, parses PT_DYNAMIC metadata, and resolves `JNI_OnLoad` through `elf_lookup`. On the crashing GNU-hash path, `elf_lookup` reads an attacker-controlled bucket head `hhead` and only checks `if (hhead)` before forming `dsp = &dynsym[hhead]`; the vulnerable source does not validate that `hhead` stays within the real dynamic symbol table before that dereference. The returned symbol pointer is then used by `PackLinuxElf64help1` to read `jni_onload_sym->st_value` through `get_te64` and `get_ne64`, producing the recorded 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow read past the end of `file_image`. The patch supports this missing-bound diagnosis by both correcting the earlier `symnum_max` computation and adding the absent `if (symnum_max <= hhead || (hhead && hhead < symbias))` check immediately before `dynsym[hhead]`.

source.description: First project statement on the witnessed path that materializes attacker-controlled ELF bytes into the heap buffer later traversed by dynamic-table and GNU-hash parsing.
source.value_from: After the sample reaches the ET_DYN-specific 64-bit ELF path, `PackLinuxElf64help1` reads the staged PoC file bytes verbatim into heap-backed `file_image`. Those attacker-controlled bytes define the dynamic segment, DT_GNU_HASH buckets, DT_SYMTAB address, and symbol records used on the crashing lookup path.

root_cause.description: Root cause on the witnessed crashing path. `elf_lookup` trusts the GNU-hash bucket head after only `if (hhead)` and forms `&dynsym[hhead]` without validating that `hhead` is within the real dynamic-symbol-table bounds.
root_cause.note: The fix commit adds `if (symnum_max <= hhead || (hhead && hhead < symbias))` immediately before this line in the 64-bit GNU-hash lookup path, and separately corrects `symnum_max` to use the actual DT_SYMTAB extent `tmp2 / sizeof(Elf64_Sym)`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `get_ne64` copies 8 bytes from the `st_value` field of a symbol pointer positioned beyond the valid `file_image` allocation.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report records `READ of size 8` at `src/bele.h:145` in `get_ne64`, reached from `BEPolicy::get64`, `Packer::get_te64`, and `PackLinuxElf64::PackLinuxElf64help1`.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific parser gate. The witness reaches the ET_DYN-specific 64-bit ELF path that reads the whole file into `file_image`, inverts PT_DYNAMIC metadata, and later resolves `JNI_OnLoad` from DT_GNU_HASH.

tainted_value_origin.description: The ET_DYN path allocates heap storage for the whole input file and fills it with the attacker-controlled ELF bytes later walked as PT_DYNAMIC, DT_GNU_HASH, and DT_SYMTAB data.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged PoC is the exact file at `gt_results/secbench_oss_upx.ossfuzz-402200343/poc`, reproduced via `./build/debug/upx -t /gt/poc`. Its bytes become `file_image`, the allocation ASan later reports as the overflowing heap region.

coarse_trace.summary: UPX accepts the staged file on the ET_DYN big-endian 64-bit ELF path, allocates `file_image`, reads the whole PoC into that heap buffer, and derives dynamic-table pointers from it.
`elf_lookup("JNI_OnLoad")` consults attacker-controlled GNU-hash metadata, reads bucket head `hhead`, and dereferences `dynsym[hhead]` after only checking that `hhead` is nonzero.
The out-of-range symbol pointer is returned as `jni_onload_sym`, then its `st_value` field is read with an 8-byte big-endian load that runs past the end of the heap-backed ELF image.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the accepted ET_DYN path, UPX copies the entire attacker-controlled ELF file into heap-backed `file_image`, creating the bytes later interpreted as PT_DYNAMIC, GNU-hash, and symbol-table data.
The copied file image is then interpreted as dynamic metadata, yielding pointers to the attacker-controlled DT_SYMTAB and DT_GNU_HASH structures that the later lookup will trust.
UPX invokes GNU-hash symbol lookup for the fixed name `JNI_OnLoad`, entering the vulnerable 64-bit lookup path with the `dynsym` and `gashtab` pointers derived from the PoC.
The PoC's DT_GNU_HASH bucket array supplies the bucket-head symbol index `hhead` for `JNI_OnLoad`. This index is attacker-controlled through the copied GNU-hash table.

The executed vulnerable-path guard only tests whether the bucket head is nonzero. On this witnessed 64-bit path, there is no bound check here to prove that `hhead` lies within the real dynamic-symbol-table extent before dereference.

Root-cause step. Because the nonzero bucket head from step 4 is trusted under step 5's narrow guard, `elf_lookup` forms a symbol pointer at index `hhead` without any source-level validation that the index stays within the actual `dynsym` allocation. The patch later inserts the missing `symnum_max`-based check immediately before this dereference.

The out-of-range `dsp` from step 6 is returned to the caller as `jni_onload_sym`, so the local symbol pointer in `PackLinuxElf64help1` now aliases memory beyond the valid `file_image` region reported by ASan.

Sink. `PackLinuxElf64help1` reads `&jni_onload_sym->st_value` through `get_te64`, `BEPolicy::get64`, and `get_ne64`, and the final 8-byte copy runs past the end of the heap-backed `file_image`, matching the recorded heap-buffer-overflow read.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The root cause is the missing GNU-hash bucket-head bounds validation before `dynsym[hhead]`, while the allocation context identifies the heap-backed `file_image` buffer from which the out-of-range symbol field is later read.

poc.trigger: Run `./build/debug/upx -t /gt/poc` on the staged testcase so UPX probes it as a 64-bit big-endian ET_DYN ELF and resolves `JNI_OnLoad` from DT_GNU_HASH / DT_SYMTAB metadata.

format.name: ELF64 big-endian shared object
format.contract: The witness must remain a 64-bit big-endian ET_DYN ELF that reaches `PackLinuxElf64ppc`, keeps the ET_DYN dynamic-parsing path alive through `PackLinuxElf64help1`, and supplies DT_GNU_HASH metadata for which lookup of `JNI_OnLoad` yields a nonzero bucket head `hhead` that is outside the real dynamic symbol table before `elf_lookup` forms `&dynsym[hhead]`. The patch text further shows that UPX intended to guard this dereference with a `symnum_max` check, but no broader numeric range is claimed beyond the witnessed metadata relationship.
